articles.title: Jay Shah re-elected unopposed as ICC chair after board clears way for bigger IPL
articles.summary: Global cricket tournaments will avoid March to May. IPL expected to expand to 12 teams from 2028. Jay Shah has been re-elected unopposed as chair of the International Cricket Council after a board meeting in Bali that has also paved the way for the expansion of the Indian Premier League.
body: In the past two years, the men’s T20 World Cup and Champions Trophy have been played in February and March. The Future Tours Programme governing bilateral series between ICC members has yet to be signed off, but sources involved in those discussions have indicated that no major series will be scheduled during those months.

Reports in India last week said that Pune and Vadodara have been earmarked as venues for new IPL franchises that would take the competition to 12 teams from 2028 and coincide with the next media rights cycle.

The Board of Cricket for Control in India (BCCI) dismissed those reports, but is believed to be exploring an expansion of the existing 10-franchise structure that would involve teams playing one another twice in the regular season, meaning 94 matches instead of 74.

In common with other major global leagues, increasing the number of fixtures for broadcasters is seen as the only way to maintain the IPL’s revenue growth after the 2024 merger of Disney and Reliance Industries to create JioStar, whose current domestic deal is worth $6bn over five years.

articles.title: Klopp says Infantino worse than Blatter
articles.summary: Germany manager Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he calls for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.
body: Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.

Infantino plans to stand for re-election in March but has been under pressure since scrapping his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.
Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for the plan but was told he was not fit to lead world football's governing body unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.
"I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," said Klopp.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland have plenty of promise but are unable to shake the self-sabotage
articles.summary: Hopes of promotion remain alive, but another costly collapse has raised familiar questions before the decisive Nations League clash with Kosovo. The Republic of Ireland stand on the verge, although of what, nobody seems quite sure.
body: This late lapse neatly captures the contradiction bedevilling this Ireland team under Hallgrímsson. Over the past 12 months, Ireland have been unmistakably better than they were during the dark days of the post-pandemic slump under Stephen Kenny. They have established a clear identity and pulled off a couple of phenomenal wins with a spine of players performing at an elite level, supplemented by emerging talent from the leagues below and beyond. Yet for all that, an acceptable level of success remains elusive for a team who have not managed to shake a maddening habit of self-sabotage.

Riding that wave of momentum, Ireland travelled to Prague last March for the playoff semi-final against Czechia, with Parrott striking again, from the penalty spot, as they set about taking an early 2-0 lead. What followed would become the lowest point of Hallgrímsson’s reign thus far, as Ireland sat back and invited pressure before conceding the needless penalty and subsequent late equaliser that preceded a crushing shootout defeat. Despite last summer’s expanded 48-team format in North America, poor game management had stymied Ireland’s chances of making the cut.

articles.title: Cop31 summit spells out stark warnings for athletes and sport organisations
articles.summary: Sport has been more visible at the latest climate crisis summit in Antalya than most others. The stakes couldn’t be higher. If Cop is the Olympics of climate diplomacy, Antalya has made getting to the starting line an event in itself.
body: Inside, the athletic achievements are less obvious. There are no world records for removing square brackets from negotiating texts, though anyone watching bleary-eyed delegations attempt it may think there should be.

Actual Olympians supplied more inspiration. I spoke alongside summer and winter athletes, including the former Swiss alpine skier and two-time Olympic champion Michelle Gisin, Sweden’s cross-country champion Charlotte Kalla, their most decorated winter Olympian, and advocacy group Adapt to Win ambassadors Danielle Alakija, who represented Fiji in the 400m at London 2012, and Kevin Wekesa, who played in the rugby sevens for Kenya at the Paris Olympics. They described how the climate crisis is reshaping the conditions in which they train and compete. Across their sports, safety, performance and the future of competition are increasingly at stake.

articles.title: Still England's best? Bronze and Earps' performances analysed
articles.summary: Sky Sports columnist Laura Hunter analyses the big talking points from the sixth round of Women's Super League matches, bringing you closer to the key stories at the heart of the women's game.
body: Nothing makes Lucy Bronze prouder than a clean sheet. She absolutely thrives off the scrap and skirmish of it. Against Manchester City, her determination to put defensive duty above all else won Chelsea a priceless three points.

Not since November 2025 had the WSL's leading scorer Khadija Shaw failed to register a shot on target in a game. Bronze can pocket that achievement. She had help from other members of the backline - Veerle Buurman was standout too - but Chelsea's captain led the lockdown.

Shaw was isolated, limited in time and space, and restricted in her movement. "We had to be like dogs in this game," Bronze told BBC Sport afterwards. "We were very focused on that." They shackled Shaw in a way few defences across Europe are able to, Bronze acting as the technical and tactical lynchpin.

This, Chelsea's biggest win of the season so far, is one that sees them leapfrog their greatest rivals in the race for this year's title. It will be a campaign built on solidity as much as anything else. The Blues have given up a miserly 0.5 goals per 90 so far.

articles.title: Camara to drive for Haas again at Las Vegas GP
articles.summary: Haas have confirmed that Rafael Camara will continue as Oliver Bearman's team-mate for this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix after making his Formula 1 debut last time out in Brazil.
body: The American-owned squad have been left with a vacant seat for the final five rounds of the season following a fallout between French driver Esteban Ocon and team boss Ayao Komatsu last month in Mexico.

Japanese driver Ryo Hirakawa, who had already featured in first practice in Mexico, drove in the Mexico City Grand Prix, before Camara, who had earlier in October been confirmed as Ocon's replacement at Haas for the 2027 season, was given the opportunity to make his debut at his home race in Sao Paulo.
The 21-year-old endured a challenging debut amid wet conditions at Interlagos, crashing out of qualifying before finishing the race last of the runners to take the chequered flag.
Komatsu said: "In Brazil, our 2027 recruit Rafa Camara made his debut under extremely challenging conditions and showed us and the world why we signed him for 2027.

articles.title: Pietersen fires England up ahead of ODI decider in Australia
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen has fired England up ahead of the ODI series decider against Australia in Hobart on Wednesday, according to fast bowler Gus Atkinson.
body: England batting great Pietersen is now a white-ball mentor with the side in a role that will run up to and including the 50-over World Cup in Africa in late 2027.
The 46-year-old will not be with the team for the winner-takes-all ODI in Tasmania, having flown to India for a YouTube conference, but gave his players some words to ponder before departing.

"KP said that winning in Australia is the best thing you can have as an England cricketer," Atkinson told reporters, with Pietersen having been part of the touring side to win the Ashes down under in 2010-11 under the captaincy of Sir Andrew Strauss.
Atkinson impressed as England levelled the ODI series in Adelaide on Sunday, bagging 4-28 as Australia were rolled for 220 chasing 356.

Frank will replace Pierre Sage, who was dismissed on November 12 following a seventh league defeat of the season to Liverpool.

articles.title: ‘I prefer not to’: Mike Brown admits he really didn’t want to do what he did during Knicks vs Raptors
articles.summary: The New York Knicks returned to winning ways with a 112-108 victory over the Toronto Raptors. The defending champions haven’t had the kind of start that they would’ve hoped for. They have won seven and lost six of their first 13 games and have shown a fair few weaknesses.
body: One of them is a lack of quality depth, and that forced Mike Brown to do something he wishes he didn’t have to against the Raptors.
Brown’s men had lost back-to-back games against the Pacers and the Cavaliers. Three defeats in a row would’ve been a terrible look, but they’ve avoided that now.
However, in order to get the win, Brown had to play Karl-Anthony Towns, Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby all for over 40 minutes.
After the game, the Knicks head coach admitted that he actually didn’t want to do that but felt that he had to.

articles.summary: Jon Rahm left the PGA Tour in order to join LIV Golf at the end of 2023. Rahm enjoyed plenty of success with LIV Golf, winning four tournaments and reigning supreme in all three of the season-long races he competed in.
body: However, the Spaniard’s decision to join LIV Golf around three years ago now looks like a really poor one.
Jon Rahm has failed to win a major championship since he joined LIV Golf. In fact, he has only one top-5 finish to his name in the majors in his last 11 starts.
With LIV Golf now on the brink of collapse, the 32-year-old will be hopeful of returning to the PGA Tour very soon indeed.
Rahm is being tipped to challenge Scottie Scheffler once again for the world number one spot, but will he be allowed to play on the PGA Tour in 2027, or will his 12-month ban be enforced?

articles.title: Cover 32: Two NFL awards are already in the bag, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 10
articles.summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into all of the biggest items from Week 10 in the NFL, including a historic day from Jahmyr Gibbs and statement return to Minnesota for Kirk Cousins
body: In lockstep with Week 10 kicking off, the second half of the regular season is underway. Naturally, there's going to be plenty of twists and turns as we barrel down the stretch run. Teams will jockey for playoff positioning while players and coaches look to put themselves in contention for awards such as MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and more. When it comes to awards, two are already in the bag.

What we saw from both of them in Week 10 only bolsters their case, if not outright putting the final nail in the coffin to eventually go home with the awards when we get to the NFL Honors during Super Bowl week.

When it comes to Monken, who opened at +1400 to win the award at DraftKings Sportsbook, he has remarkably put the Browns in the AFC playoff picture after jumping out to a 6-4 record. That record includes a 4-0 mark at home, the first time the franchise has done so since 1963.
